ai.description: The Banded Racer is a slender snake reaching 100 cm. It is olive-brown with dark, narrow crossbands on the anterior body and possesses large, prominent eyes with round pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Banded Racer is best identified by the distinct, narrow dark cross-bands on its forebody that fade into a uniform, pale olive-brown color toward the tail.
ai.habitat: The Banded Racer typically inhabits dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and open grasslands across the Indian subcontinent, generally at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Banded Racer is a highly alert, diurnal snake that actively hunts lizards and small rodents by swiftly pursuing them across open ground.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Argyrogena fasciolata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Banded Racer (*Argyrogena fasciolata*) is found across much of India, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to the southern peninsula, typically below 1,500 meters.
